findings.issue: pokemonRefsToSpecies — the central reference→species mapper (alternate-form exclusion at id < 10000, first-occurrence dedup, dex-number ordering, per-ref 'extra' payload for hidden abilities) — has no tests; a refactor to the data layer could double-count species, mislabel hidden abilities, or reorder cards with nothing failing
findings.suggestion: Add unit tests with small fixture ref lists: forms over 10000, duplicate species, slot ordering, and an is_hidden extra payload

findings.issue: The home page filter pipeline (humanized-name substring match, type-in-either-slot via pokemonTypes map, generation membership set, 48-per-page slice, page clamping) is the app's most bug-prone code and is untested; off-by-one or boolean-combination regressions would slip through
findings.suggestion: Extract the filter/paginate step into a pure function and unit-test boundary cases: empty q, page beyond last, page=0/NaN, species with a type in slot 2 only

findings.issue: Moves table construction — version-group selection defaulting to highest order, method ordering (level-up/machine/egg/tutor then alphabetical), level-up sort by level then name — is complex conditional logic with no regression guard; the alphabetize fallback rank() is exactly the kind of comparator that breaks silently
findings.suggestion: Unit-test the method-rank comparator and the per-method row sorters with mixed methods and missing power/accuracy values

findings.issue: URL-building logic is duplicated between server (index.js:94 pageUrl) and client (currentUrl); they can drift (e.g. default omission rules), and the DOM-swap enhancement (requestId race guard, catch→full-navigation fallback, popstate re-sync) has no tests — a stale-response-overwrites-newer-filter race is a classic silent bug
findings.suggestion: Share one query-serialization helper and add a Playwright test that fires rapid keystrokes and asserts the final results match the final URL

findings.issue: All display-formatting helpers — humanize (mr-mime → 'Mr Mime'), dexNumber zero-padding (#0025), formatMeasure (hectogram/dm → one decimal), latestEnglishFlavorText (last *English* entry, whitespace collapse), englishShortEffect — are pure and trivially testable but untested; the 'last English vs last entry' distinction and \f collapsing are easy to get wrong on refactor
findings.suggestion: A 30-line unit file covering these nine functions would be the highest value-per-line test in the repo

findings.issue: The promise cache caches 404s as null forever and never invalidates; plus mapPool silently leaves holes in the output array if a worker's fn rejects. Neither behavior is pinned by a test — a refactor switching to response-caching could cache rejected/error states differently
findings.suggestion: Test mapPool with a rejecting item and assert the contract (rejects, or documents hole behavior); document/verify intentional negative caching of 404

findings.issue: getPokemonTypesMap derives every Pokémon's type slots from the 18 type resources (reverse index) — an unusual construction that depends on each type's pokemon list being complete and slot-ordered; a dropped type or slot-sort regression fails nothing
findings.suggestion: Unit test against a synthetic type list: both slots present, slot ordering, and a Pokémon appearing in two types

findings.issue: Client-side sorting parses rendered textContent (Number() on cell text, '—' as missing) and flips aria-sort on click; it's coupled to rendering choices (e.g. if a cell gains a suffix like '%', numeric sort breaks) and untested for the descending-with-missing-values case
findings.suggestion: Add a Playwright test sorting a numeric column descending with em-dash rows and asserting they remain last and aria-sort flips correctly

findings.issue: Only res.status 404 maps to null; a 5xx or network failure from the API throws and there is no app test (or visible handling) for the resulting 500/crash page — the spec's 'treat the API as a live service' makes this a realistic production path
findings.suggestion: Add a test (or at least a route-level try/catch with a Not-found/error page) for API failure responses

findings.issue: Type-page moves are sorted alphabetically by humanized label while Pokémon cards sort by dex id — two orderings whose correctness is only pinned by the external suite; a locale-compare vs. codepoint-sort swap ('Flail' vs 'Flamethrower') would pass unnoticed
findings.suggestion: A one-line unit test on the label sort with names differing only after the hyphen (e.g. 'double-slap' vs 'doubleslap') would pin locale-compare semantics

summary: The agent wrote no tests of its own — every script, runner and assertion in the measured facts is zero — so all regression protection comes from the external acceptance suite it was handed. The unguarded surface is exactly where bugs live: the reference→species mapping, home-page filtering/pagination, moves-table grouping and both client-enhancement scripts. As a pull request, I'd require at least unit tests for app/src/lib/util.js and app/src/lib/data.js before merge; they're pure, cheap to test, and carry most of the app's correctness.
